"code":""""Measured LightGBM baseline for this tabular task."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd
from lightgbm import LGBMClassifier


def fit_predict(train_csv: str, test_rows: list[dict[str, str]]) -> list[float]:
    train = pd.read_csv(train_csv)
    y = train.pop("y").astype(int)
    test = pd.DataFrame(test_rows, columns=train.columns)
    for name in train.columns:
        if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(train[name]):
            test[name] = pd.to_numeric(test[name])
        else:
            categories = pd.Categorical(pd.concat([train[name], test[name]], ignore_index=True)).categories
            train[name] = pd.Categorical(train[name], categories=categories)
            test[name] = pd.Categorical(test[name], categories=categories)
    
    # Calculate scale_pos_weight based on actual class distribution
    neg_count = (y == 0).sum()
    pos_count = (y == 1).sum()
    scale_pos_weight = neg_count / pos_count
    
    model = LGBMClassifier(random_state=20261114, n_jobs=1, verbosity=-1, scale_pos_weight=scale_pos_weight)
    model.fit(train, y)
    return model.predict_proba(test)[:, 1].tolist()",
"notes":"Added scale_pos_weight=neg_count/pos_count (~5.5 for 15.5% positive rate) to LGBMClassifier to address class imbalance. This tells the model to weigh positive samples more heavily during training, which should improve recall on the minority class without changing preprocessing logic."
